title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
hints: Think about how to tell whether a number starts a sequence without sorting.
Use a hash set and only grow a sequence from values whose predecessor is absent.
For each start, walk forward while values exist; track the longest run.

title: Clone Graph
hints: You need to clone nodes and preserve edges without cloning the same node twice.
Use a map from original node to cloned node while traversing.
DFS/BFS + visited map: create the clone before recursively cloning neighbors.

title: Course Schedule
hints: Model course prerequisites as dependencies between nodes.
Ask whether the dependency graph contains a cycle.
Use DFS cycle detection or Kahn's topological sort.

title: Meeting Schedule II
hints: What determines the minimum number of rooms? Look at overlapping intervals.
Sort start and end times separately, or sort intervals and use a min-heap of end times.
The heap approach keeps the earliest finishing active meeting at the top.

title: Valid Tree
hints: A valid tree must be connected and contain no cycle.
Think graph traversal plus a condition relating edges and nodes.
For n nodes, a tree has n-1 edges; combine this with connectivity/cycle detection.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array II
hints: Binary search still works, but duplicates can make the sorted half ambiguous.
When left, middle, and right are equal, you may need to shrink the boundaries.
After resolving ambiguity, identify the sorted half and decide which side can contain the target.

title: Cheapest Flight Path
hints: This is a shortest-path problem with a limit on stops.
A standard Dijkstra state may need to include how many stops have been used.
Track cost together with stop count; relax edges while respecting the stop constraint.

title: Online Stock Span
hints: For each price, you need the nearest previous price that is strictly greater.
A monotonic decreasing stack can discard prices that can never matter again.
Store price/span pairs; pop smaller-or-equal prices and accumulate their spans.

title: Maximum Sum Circular Subarray
hints: A circular maximum is either a normal subarray or wraps around the end.
Use Kadane's algorithm for the maximum and minimum subarrays.
Answer is max(maxSubarray, totalSum - minSubarray), except when all values are negative.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
hints: A negative number can turn the smallest product into the largest.
Track both the maximum and minimum product ending at the current position.
Swap max/min when the current value is negative, then update both.

title: Majority Element II
hints: There can be at most two values occurring more than n/3 times.
Generalize Boyer-Moore voting with two candidates.
Maintain two candidates and counts, then verify the candidates in a second pass.

title: Partition Labels
hints: A partition cannot end while a character inside it appears later.
Record the last occurrence of every character.
Expand the current partition's right boundary to each character's last position.

title: Missing Number
hints: The array contains every value in [0,n] except one.
Look for an O(1)-space way to cancel matching values.
Use XOR or the arithmetic sum to recover the missing value.

title: Coin Change
hints: Think of the answer for amount x in terms of smaller amounts.
Define dp[x] as the minimum coins needed to make x.
For every amount, try each coin: dp[x] = min(dp[x], 1 + dp[x-coin]).

title: Word Break
hints: A prefix can be valid if it can be segmented into dictionary words.
Let dp[i] represent whether the prefix ending before i can be formed.
For each position, test dictionary words that could end there and transition from a valid earlier position.

title: Design Circular Queue
hints: The queue needs FIFO behavior while reusing fixed-size slots.
Track head, tail, and size (or use a sentinel slot).
Use modulo arithmetic: next index is (index + 1) % capacity.

title: House Robber
hints: At each house you either rob it or skip it.
The choice depends only on the best answers for the previous two houses.
dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + nums[i]); reduce to two variables.

title: House Robber II
hints: The first and last houses are adjacent, so you cannot take both.
Split into two linear cases: exclude first or exclude last.
Run the House Robber solution on [0,n-2] and [1,n-1].

title: 4Sum
hints: Reduce the four-number search to smaller fixed choices plus a two-pointer search.
Sort first; fix two numbers and solve a 2Sum problem on the suffix.
Skip duplicates at every fixed-pointer/two-pointer level.

title: Longest Repeating Substring with Replacement
hints: Maintain a window that can be made uniform using at most k replacements.
The key is the most frequent character inside the window.
Window is valid when windowSize - maxFrequency <= k; shrink from the left otherwise.

title: Minimum Window with Characters
hints: Find the smallest window containing all required character counts.
Use a sliding window with counts and a number of requirements currently satisfied.
Expand right until valid, then shrink left while preserving validity.

title: Time Based Key Value Store
hints: Each key has timestamped values and queries ask for the latest timestamp <= target.
Store timestamps in sorted order for each key.
Use binary search to find the rightmost timestamp not greater than the requested time.
